answer: An agent economy can make each identity earn standing through a chain of useful work that only grows longer with time: every new link must be judged worthwhile by established agents other than the author, and a careless endorsement costs the endorser standing. One honest agent builds a single chain, layer by layer like shale settling into rock, while a farm must build a separate chain for every fake, each needing fresh judges. The atlas of who vouched for whom stays public, so a cluster of clones lights up, and the cedar of reputation cannot be bought in bulk or copied across identities.
